new_commodity_proposals.evidence: Mechanically tenderized round steak, sold on a tray by the pound in the fresh beef case. Board reports ABSENT: no commodity, no capture match. Checked by food across the namespaces: the beef ids in play are ground (ground-beef-8020) and roasts; cube steak is neither, it is a thin tenderized steak at its own price per lb, and no word-order variant (cubed steak / minute steak / tenderized round steak) is carried. This is the recipe's main protein, so a null here would leave the dish uncostable.

A blended seasoning (salt, paprika, turmeric, garlic, onion) sold as an 8 oz spice-aisle bottle at several dollars, against a 26 oz salt canister at well under one. Mapping it to `salt` would be a price-class stretch of an order of magnitude. The estate already treats blended and flavoured salts as their own ids (celery-salt), and no existing id (salt, garlic-powder, paprika) covers the blend under another spelling.

registrar_rulings.reason: Swept the live feed for cube/cubed/minute/tenderized/round steak: the only 'cube' hits are Cubed Ham and Kleenex Cube boxes, and no commodity in any of the three namespaces carries an include pattern for this cut - the near rows (ribeye-steak $10.99/lb, sirloin-steak $5.49/lb, shaved-beef-steak $4.37/lb, ground-beef-8020) are same-food-different-form purchases: mechanically tenderized round is its own price class, so a new id is legitimate. Mint cube-steak in the recipe namespace (recipe-board baseline + recipe-commodities); include should cover 'cube steak', 'cubed steak', 'minute steak', 'tenderized (round|beef) steak' contiguously; excludes need ~150-pattern rigor - at minimum fence out 'steak sauce', 'steak seasoning', 'shaved', 'sirloin', 'ribeye', bouillon 'beef cubes', 'stew meat', pet food, and frozen breaded 'country fried steak' entrees; add allowlist pairs cube-steak/sirloin-steak and cube-steak/shaved-beef-steak (different cut, same food word). Separately: 'cube steaks' also needs a NEW vocabulary row (no existing name resolves) and a food-macros label transcription - none of the offered FDC rows (broth cubes) is this food.

The estate's only two 'seasoned salt' strings are EXCLUDE patterns inside garlic-herb-seasoning and sea-salt (commodities.json lines 71081 and 73807) - the neighbors deliberately refuse this product and no id claims it, so it is unpriced under every spelling; the feed prices salt at $0.0304/oz vs celery-salt at $0.415/oz, confirming blended salts are their own ~10x price class the estate already recognizes (celery-salt precedent), making this a deliberate variant, not a duplicate of salt/sea-salt/kosher-salt. Mint seasoned-salt in the recipe namespace (recipe-board baseline + recipe-commodities); include 'seasoned salt' and 'season(-| )all' (Lawry's/Morton Season-All are the shelf names but the ID stays generic); exclude plain/sea/kosher/celery/garlic salt, 'salt pork', 'seasoned black beans', snack items, bath salts, at neighbor-grade rigor; add allowlist pairs seasoned-salt/salt, seasoned-salt/sea-salt, seasoned-salt/kosher-salt, seasoned-salt/celery-salt so the daily audit never re-flags them. Separately: the vocabulary needs a new 'Seasoned Salt' name row - do NOT resolve it to the existing Salt row, whose board mapping is the order-of-magnitude price stretch the mapper flagged.

macro_cross_check: Source publishes 687 cal / 18 carbs / 42 protein over 4 servings. Recomputed at source scale: about 1,368 cal and 50 g protein per serving. TWO gaps, both explainable and both worth a person's eye. (1) Calories: 701 of those 1,368 are the 1 1/2 cups of frying oil counted in full. Shallow-fry oil is a cooking medium - maybe 3 to 4 tbsp is actually absorbed - so the honest eaten figure is around 660 to 700 cal, right on the source's 687 and inside this run's 400-650 band only marginally. As the table stands the recipe will compute at roughly double the cap and will be retired on paper. I did not override the settled vegetable-oil weight, because the full 327 g is what the shopper buys; the fix is a cooking-loss basis, not a smaller purchase. (2) Protein 50 g against 42, +20%: the buttermilk soak, the egg wash and most of the dredge flour are drained or shaken off, so the coating is counted whole when only part of it fries onto the steak. Cube steak alone gives about 33 g per serving, which sits sensibly under the published 42 once the adhering coating and gravy milk are added. No portion looks wrong; the basis does.
